title: Developer Economics and Ecosystem Plugins Roadmap — Q1 2029
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:

This document describes the strategic roadmap, core requirements (PRD), high-level design decisions, and commercialization plan for the Developer Economics and Ecosystem Plugins initiative for Q1 2029. The initiative aims to grow developer adoption, monetize third-party plugin integrations, and surface actionable consumption insights so product teams can optimize cost/latency tradeoffs for developer-led workloads.

Why this initiative now:
- We observe a 45% year-over-year growth in API signups but only 12% conversion to paid tiers for plugin-enabled flows.
- Customers have requested a clearer way to attach third-party plugin costs to consumption and to receive packaged pricing for plugin-enabled workflows.
- Enabling an ecosystem of plugins increases stickiness and drives higher average revenue per developer (ARPD) if we provide clear commercial primitives and telemetry.

Goals (success criteria):
1. Increase paid conversion for developer accounts that try plugins from 12% to 22% within six months of GA.
2. Launch a plugin billing primitive and attribution surface that yields >= 90% cost-allocation accuracy for plugin-invoked tokens.
3. Integrate consumption telemetry into Console insights for plugin flows with < 2.5% sampling overhead.
4. Introduce two commercial plugin packaging options and secure pilot customers for each (at least 3 pilots).

Scope and out-of-scope:
- In scope: hosted plugin registry, per-plugin consumption attribution, new packaging SKUs for plugin-augmented routes, Console UX for plugin economics, SDK hooks for plugin tracing, and a billing export for partner settlements.
- Out of scope: on-prem/private plan billing adapters (handled in a later wave), marketplace payments processing, and fully managed plugin hosting (partners self-host).

Principles guiding design:
- Developer-first: minimal friction to try and compose plugins from the Console and SDK.
- Transparent economics: customers should see line-item plugin cost impact in the same flow as model tokens.
- Low overhead: telemetry and attribution must not add measurable latency to the critical path.
- Composability: support multi-plugin chains with deterministic attribution heuristics.

Roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- Q1 2029 (this doc):
  - Finalize plugin billing primitive spec and attribution algorithm.
  - Build plugin registry MVP with metadata and verification tags.
  - Implement SDK tracing hooks and Console consumption insights for plugin flows (beta).
  - Define two packaging SKUs: Plugin-Add-on (per-call marginal), and Plugin-Bundle (monthly seat + capped tokens).
  - Begin partner pilots (3 selected ISVs).

- Q2 2029:
  - GA plugin registry and billing primitive; enable per-plugin line items in invoices.
  - Launch partner settlement export and pilot partner payout templates.
  - Add predictive cost estimates to Console for plugin-enabled routes.

- Q3 2029:
  - Integrate plugin consumption insights into Optimize recommendations.
  - Expand packaging templates and self-serve partner onboarding.

- Success metrics to track each quarter:
  - Paid conversion uplift for plugin-enabled developer cohorts.
  - Accuracy of plugin cost attribution vs partner-reported usage.
  - Latency overhead introduced by tracing (P95).
  - Number of pilots converted to commercial contracts.

PRD: core requirements (brief):
A. Billing primitive and attribution algorithm (MUST):
   - Assign token consumption and runtime costs to the invoking plugin(s) with deterministic rules for multi-plugin chains (e.g., last-invoker wins, or weighted by time-in-plugin).
   - Provide an API to fetch attributed consumption per-tenant, per-route, per-plugin for arbitrary date ranges.
   - Ensure attribution accuracy > 90% on synthetic tests and > 85% on production shadow runs.

B. SDK and runtime hooks (MUST):
   - SDKs (JS, Python) expose a simple plugin invocation API that attaches plugin_id and correlation_id to requests.
   - Runtime accepts plugin metadata and emits a lightweight trace event at plugin entry/exit.

C. Registry and verification (SHOULD):
   - Registry stores plugin metadata: name, vendor, semantic tags, cost model (per-call or per-token), verification status, docs link.
   - Allow partners to self-submit manifests and request verification badges.

D. Console & telemetry (MUST):
   - Console shows per-plugin consumption, estimated token cost, percent of total route spend, and trend charts.
   - Provide downloadable CSV/JSON exports suitable for finance reconciliation.

E. Pricing & packaging (MUST/SHOULD):
   - Define two SKU families: per-call marginal (Plugin-Add-on) and subscription bundles (Plugin-Bundle).
   - Pricing rules must allow: per-tenant overrides, trial credits, and per-plugin revenue share settings for partner settlements.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- Attribution model: deterministic weighting vs probabilistic sampling. Deterministic models are easier to reason about for billing but can misattribute in complex async plugin graphs. We will implement a deterministic last-invoker weighting with a later plan to support time-weighted attribution for long-running plugins.

- Telemetry overhead: trace events should be encoded in compact binary and sampled at a low default rate (1%) with an adjustable tenant-level sample rate. For billing accuracy we run deterministic attribution on all billed requests but run tracing only for diagnostics.

- Security and confidentiality: plugins may receive user data. The registry will surface a "data sensitivity" flag and partners must declare processing requirements. Billing metadata must not leak customer PII; only plugin_id and cost metrics are stored in billing exports.

Pricing & packaging (commercial brief):
- Plugin-Add-on (per-call marginal):
  - Charged on top of standard token costs. Simple per-call fee or per-token multiplier published in registry.
  - Ideal for low-frequency, high-value integrators (e.g., external search, knowledge connectors).
  - Billing flow: plugin fee + tokens consumed by plugin + base route tokens.

- Plugin-Bundle (subscription):
  - Monthly seat or route-level subscription that bundles a token allowance and plugin runtime credits. Overage rates apply above allowance.
  - Discounts for annual contracts and for multi-plugin bundles.
  - Offer a standard contract template for partner revenue share (e.g., 70/30 split after threshold).

- Pilot commercial terms (Q1):
  - Offer partners 6-month pilot with waived listing fees, reduced 10% revenue share for first 3 months, and co-marketing credit.

Console UX and developer flows (high level):
1. Discover: Developer navigates registry, reads plugin docs and cost model.
2. Try: Click "Try in sandbox" launches quick demo with sample tenant credits.
3. Instrument: SDK call attaches plugin metadata and correlation id.
4. Observe: Console insights display plugin cost breakdown and allow exporting the data.
5. Commercialize: In Console, enable "Add plugin bundle" to route and buy the SKU.

Launch plan (detailed Q1 -> GA):
1. Beta (internal + partners) — weeks 1–8:
   - Release registry MVP and SDK hooks to partners; enable shadow billing exports for validation.
   - Run synthetic tests and two partner pilots.

2. Public beta — weeks 9–16:
   - Open registry to limited developers, add Console insights, enable trial SKUs.
   - Collect feedback and refine attribution heuristics.

3. GA (target by end of Q2):
   - Turn on billing primitive for paying tenants, publish official docs and contract templates, enable partner settlement exports.

Rollout and rollback steps (operational):
1. Feature flags: all components behind feature flags scoped by tenant.
2. Shadow mode: run attribution in shadow for 2–4 weeks before billing activation.
3. Monitor: Key alerts — attribution mismatch rate >10%, sample trace latency P95 increase >10ms, Console export failures >0.5%.
4. Rollback: disable billing routing and revert tenant flag; schedule hotfix and run tenant reconciliation.

Open questions for leadership (to resolve before Q1 dev start):
- Acceptable default revenue share for partner plugin bundles (proposal: 70/30 after $X threshold).
- Minimum attribution accuracy threshold required for switching from shadow to billed mode (proposal: 90%).
- Tolerance for Console sampling overhead (proposal: default 1%, configurable).

Risks and mitigations:
- Misattribution causing billing disputes: mitigate with extended shadow runs, partner reconciliation exports, and a 30-day safe window where invoices are informational only.
- Latency regressions from tracing: use sampling and offload heavy telemetry work to async pipelines.
- Partner fraud / misdeclared cost models: implement registry verification badges and periodic partner audits.

Appendix: short tables and examples

Example attribution CSV columns (export):
| tenant_id | route_id | plugin_id | date | token_count | plugin_cost_usd | attribution_method | correlation_id |
| 12345 | chat.route.create | plugin.search.v1 | 2029-01-05 | 420 | 0.36 | deterministic-last-invoker | abc-123 |

Sample SDK call (JS):
```
const res = await Redwood.plugins.invoke({
  plugin_id: 'plugin.search.v1',
  correlation_id: 'abc-123',
  input: {
    prompt: 'Summarize meeting notes',
  }
});
```

Next steps (this week):
1. Product to confirm revenue share floor with finance and partnerships.
2. Engineering to draft the billing primitive API and estimate implementation effort (T-shirt sizing).
3. Partnerships to identify candidate pilots and prepare initial manifests.
